weBeat: visual: an estimation plot in the user's own units (every value as a dot, the mean of each group with its interval, grey lines for pairs, and the difference with its interval against a zero line) next to the t curve; Stats Kingdom draws only the abstract t curve, the others draw nothing

functional: Welch and pooled results side by side from the same data with a plain-English note on which fits and whether they disagree; a 'What would it take' table (smallest difference that would be significant, people needed for p below alpha, power of this test, people needed for 80% power) with exact noncentral-t power; all three comparisons (two groups, before and after, one group) in one page with raw numbers or summary numbers (mean, SD or SEM, n); t-score and degrees of freedom only mode

every competitor feature kept except Chicago citation style, CSV / Excel file upload, R code, Print, last-run restore and the Shapiro-Wilk normality test (dropped under his approval of the research report, recorded in the parity file)
unverified: Copy buttons in a real clipboard session
normality is not tested (no Shapiro-Wilk): the page shows skewness, outliers and the dots instead
no rule-of-thumb labels for Cohen's d (no primary source read)
power and people-needed counts assume equal group sizes and the observed difference; checked against an independent integration, not against another calculator

the competitors were compared from the research pass and the same pages reloaded after the build, not typed side by side with every input; the example data gave the same t, df, p and interval as Social Science Statistics and Stats Kingdom
